Δ, a sum of absolute differences of binomial means, is not a polynomial in the probabilities, so no estimator is unbiased for it, whatever the counts; bias can be reduced, not removed. The squared difference is unbiasedly estimable, and its root halves the plug-in's bias where signalling is small, at a cost where it is large. What can be stated is an error: simultaneous Clopper-Pearson intervals for every marginal give an interval for Δ valid at any count, and exact per-content tests, combined by Bonferroni, give a test of the null that no content signals. Neither can say anything from one or two occurrences a context. This answers the estimator half of [CLAIM-235](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-235.md)'s request; the data half waits on counts [LIT-851](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-851.md) does not print.
